newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Sihanouk stresses he had no interest in politics.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk stresses he had no interest in politics.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk has said politicians' fears he may return to politics before general elections in 1998 are "ridiculous" and reflect distrust of his pledge of neutrality.

The king did not mention any names, but co-Premier Hun Sen on March 14 warned that he would cancel local and general elections due in 1997 and 1998 if Sihanouk abdicated and decided to take part in politics.

Analysts believe Hun Sen and his ex-communist Cambodian People's Party, which formed an uneasy alliance with the royalist FUNCINPEC party after the U.N.-run polls in 1993, fear Sihanouk would win elections on the back of his grass roots popularity if he stepped down from the throne.

The king, in an interview conducted on Friday and released by the palace on Saturday, said he was flattered by those senior personalities and parties who were scared of his entering the political arena.

"But I am disappointed that they consider me a liar when I give and regive formal assurance of non-engagement (total and irreversible) of Norodom Sihanouk in political life, legislative and other elections in Cambodia and of my total neutrality towards the Cambodian political parties," he said.

The 74-year old monarch reiterated that expert astrologers in Hong Kong and Paris had said he would not live beyond 1997 and he noted that his latest medical bulletin from March this year showed he suffers from many serious ailments.
"Even if the heavens grant me the favour to live longer than that, I would not lie to my people. And I have never been unfaithful to my given word," he said.
Sihanouk concluded that "the fear that certain of my compatriot politicians feel about the possiblity of my political activities in the framework of the legislative elections of 1998 is ridiculous."

The king, who reigns but does not rule, sparked a crisis over the monarchy and elections when he said in February he was considering abdicating because of mounting attacks on himself and the royal family.
